headline: High-risk default workflow automation can leak data and trigger unsafe downstream actions when paired with a support bot.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow inputs and files, and Rasa consumes text/voice messages from channels like Slack and Telegram. If Rasa output is routed into n8n without sanitization, attacker-controlled chat content can become workflow instructions. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and not proven.
conditions: IF Rasa messages are forwarded into an n8n workflow step as plain text
IF n8n workflow nodes interpret that text as commands or prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Add an explicit allowlist parser for inbound bot text
Insert a human review step before any command-like action
Strip markdown, code fences, and imperative phrases from bot outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between Rasa and n8n
requires-engineering: isolate untrusted chat content in a separate queue

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has server filesystem access and broad network egress, while Rasa handles text and voice and can connect to external messaging platforms. In a shared workflow, sensitive content processed by n8n can be forwarded into Rasa channels or logs. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default automation setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF n8n workflows process sensitive files or secrets
IF those outputs are sent into Rasa-connected channels or stored in shared logs
mitigations: Minimize data passed from n8n to Rasa to redacted summaries
Disable verbose logging on both sides for sensitive workflows
Use separate credentials and workspaces for each system
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce retention limits on shared transcripts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Rasa is a separate chatbot stack with multiple channel integrations. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared integration credentials, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or race on shared resources. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or credential store
IF the orchestrator does not provide file or job locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories and credential stores
Run each agent under distinct OS users
Avoid shared mutable config files
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources
requires-engineering: move shared state to an atomic datastore

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an automation orchestrator that can execute commands and API calls, while Rasa produces dialogue outputs for downstream handling. If n8n treats Rasa responses as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious bot reply can cascade into emails, API calls, or file writes. Because n8n defaults include action-taking and no verification is documented, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF n8n uses Rasa output as the trigger for an action node
IF there is no verification or approval step before the action node
mitigations: Add a confirmation gate before any side-effecting node
Require structured outputs with schema validation
Log and review bot-to-automation handoffs
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before execution
requires-engineering: separate suggestion generation from execution

E_compliance.rationale: n8n explicitly handles secrets and workflow data on its server, while Rasa processes text and voice and integrates with third-party messaging platforms. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the same regulated data class flows through both systems. No certifications or DPA details are provided, so the safest supported severity is medium.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through both systems
IF their retention or residency settings differ for that data class
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between systems
Disable storage of unnecessary transcripts
Align retention settings across both platforms
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows for shared records
